name: Territorial 3-5-2 Wing-Back

slots.why: Sweeps behind a higher back three, so the space behind it is covered without dropping the line.
Starts possession with the short goalkeeper outlet, then defends the left channel behind the attacking wing-back. FM20 has no Wide Centre-Back role.
Stays central and covers behind the outside defenders and attacking wing-backs. Defend is the alternate for a defender better suited to holding the line.
Defends the right channel behind the attacking wing-back while the central Cover defender protects the space behind the three.
The only width on the left: he lives in the opponent's half, pinning their wide player and crossing from the byline.
Screens the back three and wins the second ball at the edge of the opponent's box when the team attacks.
Counter-presses on the left and arrives in the box as the third attacker behind the two forwards.
Recycles possession after each regain and switches play to the wing-back with the most space.
The only width on the right: he lives in the opponent's half, pinning their wide player and crossing from the byline.
Leads the press on the centre-backs and drops in to link play, then joins his partner in the box when the cross comes.
Attacks the near post and the space behind the centre-backs. Poacher is the alternate for a striker who stays in the box.

description: A positive 3-5-2 that holds territory with two attacking wing-backs, a counter-press and two forwards plus a midfield runner meeting the deliveries.
whyGood: Attacking wing-backs supply the width, with two forwards and a runner attacking deliveries. Three centre-backs and a holding midfielder provide cover behind that pressure.
whyThisShape: The wing-backs supply the attacking width in this FM20 version. Three centre-backs cover behind them: a left Ball-Playing Defender starts the build-up, the right Central Defender protects his channel, and the central Cover defender reads the space behind both. The higher defensive and engagement lines support the counter-press. The holder screens the defence, the deep playmaker recycles possession, and the box-to-box midfielder joins the pressing forward and Advanced Forward around the box. Slightly shorter passing connects the midfield; with neither Counter nor Hold Shape selected, the team chooses how to use each regain. The outside centre-backs are not instructed to overlap: the specialised Wide Centre-Back role belongs to later FM editions.
whenToUse: Against weaker sides that defend deep and clear their lines, when you have two attacking wing-backs, three centre-backs who can protect their channels, and two useful forwards.
whenNotToUse: With wing-backs who cannot sustain the running, against wingers who will attack the space behind them, or against a side with quick forwards who run behind a higher line.
whenLeading: Keep the supporting central platform while assessing the pressure and the wing-backs. Replace tired wide players before they stop recovering; dropping the entire block is a separate in-match decision, not an automatic consequence of taking the lead.

instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Challenge immediately after losing possession, with the roles around the ball supporting the first pressure.
instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Engage the build-up earlier, accepting that the forwards need support from the midfield behind them.
instructionRationale.Higher Defensive Line: Move the back line up to reduce the space behind the midfield and support territorial pressure.
instructionRationale.More Urgent Pressing: Challenge more often inside the selected engagement zone without making the settled press maximal.
instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Slightly Shorter Passing: Retain connected passing options while still allowing progression into the forward line.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: To the near post and penalty spot for two forwards and the arriving midfielder.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: Keeps the pressure on when ahead.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Centre Backs: Start through the back three, with the left Ball-Playing Defender providing the more ambitious first pass.
instructionRationale.Roll It Out: Keeps goal kicks and catches in the team's possession.

keyRequirements: Two wing-backs with the stamina to cover a whole flank and the crossing to finish moves
Three centre-backs who protect the channels, including a ball-player and a covering defender
A holding midfielder who screens and reads second balls
A pressing forward who links play and a striker who attacks the near post
Stamina and work rate across midfield and attack
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.

FM20 compatibility correction: BPD (Defend) left, CD (Cover) centre, CD (Defend) right replace the previously listed outer Wide Centre-Back roles, which were introduced in FM22. The wing-backs now supply the attacking width; this is a revised template.
